paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.
model_annotation: The diagram displays empirical generalization errors (labeled “Errors (BoolQ)”) as a function of adapter rank, which corresponds to the hidden dimension size used in fine-tuning adapters on the Llama-3-8B model. The x-axis is labeled “Rank” and uses a linear scale ranging from 4 to 256, with tick marks at regular intervals of 12 (specifically at 4, 16, 64, and 256), representing the adapter’s hidden dimension size. The y-axis is labeled “Errors (BoolQ)” and also uses a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 0.6, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. A single black line connects four data points, each marked with a solid green circle, representing the error values at each rank: starting at approximately 0.27 at rank 4, decreasing to approximately 0.23 at rank 16, increasing to approximately 0.30 at rank 64, and rising further to approximately 0.36 at rank 256. Each data point is accompanied by a vertical error bar indicating uncertainty, with the bars appearing roughly symmetric around the data point.

model_annotations.English: This line plot illustrates the empirical generalization errors, labeled “Errors (BoolQ)”, for fine-tuned adapters using QAdapter on the Llama-3-8B model, plotted against different adapter ranks. The x-axis, labeled “Rank”, is logarithmic and spans the values 4, 16, 64, and 256, representing the hidden dimension sizes of the adapters. The y-axis, labeled “Errors (BoolQ)”, is linear and ranges from 0.0 to 0.6, indicating the error rate on the BoolQ dataset. A single black line with circular green markers connects the data points, showing that the error starts at approximately 0.26 at Rank 4, dips slightly to about 0.23 at Rank 16, rises to roughly 0.30 at Rank 64, and then increases further to approximately 0.35 at Rank 256. Each data point is accompanied by a vertical error bar, indicating the uncertainty or variability in the measured error.
